question.text: Which of the following is NOT an eligible investment/expenditure for deduction under Section 80C?

answer.text: Life insurance premium paid for self, spouse and children
Health insurance premium paid for self and family
Principal repayment of a housing loan

explanation.text: The Logic: Health/medical insurance premium is deductible under Section 80D, not Section 80C. The workbook places medical insurance squarely under 80D, while 80C covers items such as life insurance premium, principal repayment of a housing loan, and small-saving schemes; Sukanya Samriddhi receipts are also recognised as tax-favoured under Section 10(11A). The distinction between 80C (investment/savings-linked) and 80D (health insurance) is the point being tested. The Trap: All three distractors are 80C-eligible items in the workbook list. Health insurance premium feels like it could be a savings-style deduction, but it has its own dedicated section (80D). Note: Keep a mental separation between 80C (investments and savings) and 80D (health insurance). Life insurance premium goes under 80C; health insurance premium goes under 80D.
